# edge-api

Stateless edge API

## Permanent rules

These rules apply to every intervention, whatever the file. Details and anti-patterns are in the `workflow` skill.

- **CORE-001** — Before any non-trivial change (more than one file, a schema change, or a new dependency), the agent writes a short plan and waits for confirmation.
- **CORE-002** — One task is one coherent change and one commit; refactoring and features are never mixed in the same commit.
- **CORE-003** — The agent never creates `WIP`, `tmp` or `fix later` commits; a change is committed only once its tests pass.
- **CORE-004** — Tests are written in the same change as the code they cover, never in a later commit.
- **CORE-005** — When the specification is ambiguous or contradictory, the agent stops and asks; it does not pick the most likely interpretation.
- **CORE-006** — Adding a dependency is a separate commit that follows the profile's dependency procedure.
- **CORE-007** — The agent never runs `git push`, `git reset --hard` or `git clean`.
- **CORE-040** — Code identifiers (namespaces, classes, methods, variables, columns) are always in English.
- **CORE-041** — Comments and documentation are written in the project's configured language (see the project settings section).
- **CORE-042** — Business terms are defined in `docs/glossary.md` and reused verbatim in identifiers, in their English form.

## Skills

One skill per topic. Every rule carries a stable identifier (`NET-002`) to quote in plans and reviews.

| Skill | Covers | File |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture` | Projects, namespaces, dependency direction and the reference example of the project. Read before creating a class or adding a reference. | `.claude/skills/architecture/SKILL.md` |
| `db` | Entities, `DbContext`, repositories, transactions and EF Core migrations. Read before touching the schema or persistence. | `.claude/skills/db/SKILL.md` |
| `api` | Controllers, DTOs, `ProblemDetails`, pagination and versioning. Read before exposing or changing an endpoint. | `.claude/skills/api/SKILL.md` |
| `testing` | The three test levels, Testcontainers, naming. Read before writing or changing a test. | `.claude/skills/testing/SKILL.md` |
| `workflow` | Plan, commits, dependencies, language and forbidden commands. The agent's working contract. | `.claude/skills/workflow/SKILL.md` |
| `security` | Secrets, health endpoints, CORS, headers, dependency scanning and the security option of the project. Read before touching configuration or authentication. | `.claude/skills/security/SKILL.md` |

## How to read a rule

Each rule is one verifiable sentence followed by its rationale. The marker after the identifier says who enforces it:

- `compiler`: the project reference does not exist, the build fails. `arch-test`, `analyzer`, `format`, `ef-migrations`, `nuget-audit`, `commitlint`, `gitleaks`: tooled constraint, the build or the commit fails when it is violated.
- `guidance`: a rule of conduct for the agent, checked in review, with no tool behind it.

## Commands

- `dotnet build` — compiles the solution, analyzers included
- `dotnet test` — the three test levels and the NetArchTest rules
- `dotnet test --filter Category!=Integration` — the same, without Docker
- `dotnet format` — formats the code (run before every commit)
- `prepwork sync` — updates generated files after a change to `scaffold.yaml`

## File ownership

- Files listed in `.scaffold/manifest.json` are generated: do not edit them, they would be overwritten or reported by `prepwork sync`.
- `docs/adr/`, `docs/glossary.md` and all business code belong to the team and are never in the manifest.
- The reference example (`Note`) is generated; deleting or changing it is a team choice, `sync` reports it and never recreates it.

## Git

- Commit author: `Jane <jane@example.com>`
- Agent commits carry no co-author trailer.
- Forbidden to the agent: `git push`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean`.
